R: instrument_description: Section 38(ण): it is an offence to produce, sell or distribute any goods that the Government of Nepal has, by notice published in the Nepal Gazette, banned as being goods that cause excessive waste generation ("फोहरमैला अत्यधिक उत्पादन हुने वस्तु भनी नेपाल सरकारले नेपाल राजपत्रमा सूचना प्रकाशन गरी प्रतिबन्ध लगाएको कुनै वस्तुको उत्पादन तथा बिक्री वितरण गर्ने"); Section 39(10) empowers the Chief District Officer to fine an offender NPR 5,000-10,000 and/or imprison them for up to 3 months for breach of any such ban.
U: instrument_implementation_text: Authority explicit (Government of Nepal designates banned goods by Gazette notice; Chief District Officer enforces) (+0.25); enforcement explicit (fine and/or imprisonment under Section 39(10)) (+0.25); the ban applies to whatever goods are gazetted with no further statutory exemption (+0.25 unconditional); no explicit monitoring/inspection mechanism is attached to this specific offence clause (0).
W: comments: This is the specific statutory hook by which Nepal has, in practice, banned thin single-use plastic bags: the underlying power is an enabling one (a ban only exists once the Government of Nepal has gazetted a specific product as an 'excessive-waste-generating good'), but it has been operationalised through subordinate instruments -- most recently the Plastic Bags (Regulation and Control) Directive, 2082 (2025/26) issued by the Ministry of Forests and Environment -- so it is coded in force (S=1) per Rule 12's test for an enabling power that has already been exercised. This is the only provision across the four Nepali instruments coded so far that maps onto a conventional single-use-plastic ban; recommend cross-referencing the Plastic Bags (Regulation and Control) Directive, 2082 as a distinct subordinate instrument in any future update to this index.
